

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r}
english_sample1_A <- read_csv(here("data/ratings","english_sample1.csv")) # all dimensions
english_sample1_B <- read_csv(here("data/ratings", "english_sample1_redo.csv")) # all dimensions
english_sample1_C <- read_csv(here("data/ratings","english_sample1_redo2.csv")) # all dimensions

english_sample1 <- english_sample1_A %>% 
  full_join(english_sample1_B) %>%
  full_join(english_sample1_C) %>% distinct()

ALL_df_BUCLD <- read_csv(here("data/ratings", "ALL_df_BUCLD.csv")) # all dimensions
```

🔧 Step 1: Align columns

```{r}
# 1. Keep only the shared columns
common_cols <- intersect(names(ALL_df_BUCLD), names(english_sample1))
df1 <- ALL_df_BUCLD[, common_cols]
df2 <- english_sample1[, common_cols]

# 2. Reorder columns to be in the same order
df1 <- df1[, common_cols]
df2 <- df2[, common_cols]

# 3. Arrange both for consistent row order (optional, for cleaner diff)
df1 <- dplyr::arrange_all(df1)
df2 <- dplyr::arrange_all(df2)

```

🔎 Step 2: Find overlaps and differences

```{r}
# Use dplyr's anti_join and intersect logic

library(dplyr)

# Rows present in BOTH
common_rows <- intersect(df1, df2)

# Rows only in ALL_df_BUCLD
only_in_BUCLD <- anti_join(df1, df2)

# Rows only in english_sample1
only_in_english <- anti_join(df2, df1)

```

# sample 2

```{r}
english_sample2_A <- read_csv(here("data/ratings","english_sample2.csv")) # only category

english_sample2_B <- read_csv(here("data/ratings", "english_sample2_redo1.csv")) 
english_sample2_C <- read_csv(here("data/ratings","english_sample2_redo3.csv")) 
english_sample2_D <- read_csv(here("data/ratings","english_sample2_redo4.csv")) 


english_sample2 <- english_sample2_A %>% 
  full_join(english_sample2_B) %>%
  full_join(english_sample2_C)  %>%
  full_join(english_sample2_D) %>% 
  distinct()
```

🔧 Step 1: Align columns

```{r}
# 1. Keep only the shared columns
common_cols_sample2 <- intersect(names(ALL_df_BUCLD), names(english_sample2))
df1_sample2 <- ALL_df_BUCLD[, common_cols_sample2]
df2_sample2 <- english_sample2[, common_cols_sample2]

# 2. Reorder columns to be in the same order
df1_sample2 <- df1_sample2[, common_cols_sample2]
df2_sample2 <- df2_sample2[, common_cols_sample2]

# 3. Arrange both for consistent row order (optional, for cleaner diff)
df1_sample2 <- dplyr::arrange_all(df1_sample2)
df2_sample2 <- dplyr::arrange_all(df2_sample2)

```

🔎 Step 2: Find overlaps and differences

```{r}

# Rows present in BOTH
common_rows_sample2 <- intersect(df1_sample2, df2_sample2)
write_csv(common_rows_sample2, here("data/ratings", "correct_english_sample2.csv"))

# Rows only in ALL_df_BUCLD
only_in_BUCLD_sample2 <- anti_join(df1_sample2, df2_sample2)

# Rows only in english_sample1
only_in_english_sample2 <- anti_join(df2_sample2, df1_sample2)

```

```{r}
intersect(only_in_english_sample2, english_sample1)

# Rows present in BOTH
intersect(english_sample1, only_in_BUCLD_sample2)

# Rows only in english_sample1
anti_join(english_sample1, only_in_BUCLD_sample2)

# Rows only in ALL_df_BUCLD
anti_join(only_in_BUCLD_sample2, english_sample1)

english_sample1 <- english_sample1  %>% 
  full_join(only_in_BUCLD_sample2) %>% 
  distinct()

write_csv(english_sample1, here("data/ratings", "correct_english_sample1.csv"))

```
